#!/bin/sh
# Validate monthly data files before they are committed.
exec python3 - <<'PY'
import csv, glob, sys
year = open("scripts/check.conf").read().split("=", 1)[1].strip()
files = sorted(glob.glob(f"data/{year}-*.csv"))
for path in files:
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    header = rows[0]
    for n, row in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):
        if len(row) != len(header):
            print(f"{path}: row {n} has {len(row)} fields, expected {len(header)}")
            sys.exit(1)
print("OK")
PY

content.text:
I copied `inbox/2025-12.csv` to `data/2025-12.csv` and committed it as `2025-12: add rows`. The commit adds 32 lines.

`scripts/check.sh` passed before the commit. I made sure the check actually covered the new file: it only looks at files for the year set in `scripts/check.conf`, which is 2025, so December was included.

I left the original in `inbox/` because git doesn't track that folder and the earlier monthly commits never touched it. You can delete it yourself if you don't need it.

The check will stop covering new files in January. Once 2026 files arrive, `check.sh` will skip them until someone changes `year=2025` in `scripts/check.conf`.
